beginner.summary: For developers, testers and junior DevOps engineers who have used Git and a build tool but have never administered or configured JetBrains TeamCity. Covers the server, agent and web UI model, running TeamCity On-Premises in Docker and a first look at TeamCity Cloud, projects and build configurations, Git VCS roots, Command Line, Gradle and Maven runners, parameters and build numbers, artifacts, VCS and schedule triggers, test reporting and service messages, failure conditions, feature branches, agent authorization and requirements, templates, notifications, users and roles, and a capstone that builds, tests and packages a Java service end to end.
prerequisites: Uses Git from the command line to clone, branch, commit and push to a hosted repository such as GitHub or GitLab
Can build and test a project locally with at least one build tool such as Gradle, Maven, npm or dotnet
Has a laptop with Docker Desktop or Docker Engine, 8 GB of free RAM and rights to open port 8111 on localhost
outcomes: Run a TeamCity server and an authorized build agent in Docker and navigate projects, build configurations and build results
Create build configurations with Git VCS roots, runners, parameters, artifact paths and build number formats
Trigger builds from commits, schedules and other builds, filter branches and report tests and problems through service messages
Reuse settings with templates, control which agents run builds and grant project roles to users and groups
